correctness.rationale: PASS. The weighted Bergman orthonormal basis is E_u(z)=sqrt((ν)_{|u|}/u!) z^u with ν=n+α+1. Unitarily rotate ξ to e1; the kernel power series and positivity of μ give C E_u as a sum over j≥0 with moment μ_{|u|+j}, coefficient (β)_j/j!, and monomial norm ratio sqrt[(ν)_{|u|}/(ν)_{|u|+j} × (u1+j)!/u1!]. Orthogonality of different multiindices in each image and Tonelli collapse the basis squared norms. Summing (u1+j)!/u1! over |u|=k via j!(1-x)^(-j-1)(1-x)^(-(n-1)) yields exactly S_m. This identity is an iff for the polynomial operator's S2 extension, not an assertion of unboundedness otherwise. Write S_m as Γ(m+n)/Γ(m+ν) times convolution d_j*g_{m-j}; d_j~j^(2β-n-1)/Γ(β)^2, g_k~k^(n+α). For 2β<n dominated convergence gives m^(n-1)∑d_j; equality gives a harmonic log; 2β>n gives the Beta integral and m^(2β-1). Positive leading constants imply all displayed moment tests. For μ_{s,r}, Laplace substitution gives Γ(s)m^(-s)(log m)^(-r); integral test supplies sharp r>1/2 or r>1 critical cutoffs. Independently recomputed critical n=2,α=0,β=1 coefficients S_m=1,7/3,47/12,57/10,153/20,341/35 with exact rational arithmetic. Finite coefficients do not establish asymptotics.
